# Music API migration

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/music/legacy

Use the current background music-generation API; distinguish unfinished specialized outcomes from retired REST paths.

## Generate a song now

Use [`POST /api/music`](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/music/generate) with a prompt and lyrics.
It returns `202` with a generation record; poll
[`GET /api/music/{generationId}`](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/music/get) for completion and
the resulting audio URL. It does not return audio in the initial response.
See the current reference for accepted settings, account scope and credits.

## Former music routes

The six POST paths below are retired from the callable specification because
they have no implemented handlers in the current API. They are not aliases for
`POST /api/music`. Their specialized outcomes are not equivalent to ordinary
song generation and are not declared canceled by this correction.

| Former path | Current choice and remaining limit |
| --- | --- |
| `/api/music/compose` | Use the current generation API for a prompt-and-lyrics song. Composition-plan input and an immediate binary-audio response are not supported replacements. |
| `/api/music/compose/detailed` | Use generation status/result reads for the fields actually returned. Multipart audio and word-level timestamps are not established by that result. |
| `/api/music/plan` | No hosted structured-composition-plan replacement is established. A locally prepared plan is not a supported request field, and the old free-operation claim is withdrawn. |
| `/api/music/stream` | Poll for the completed audio URL. The current API does not establish playback of partial audio chunks while the song is generated. |
| `/api/music/video-to-music` | No hosted upload-video-to-soundtrack replacement is established. Do not send video files to the prompt-and-lyrics endpoint. |
| `/api/music/stem-separation` | No hosted stem-separation replacement is established. Generating a new song does not split an existing recording into stems. |

## What remains undecided

[Reconciliation #327](https://github.com/recoupable/mono/issues/327) retains the
specialized capability decisions. The current music-generation implementation
is tracked in [App #1992](https://github.com/recoupable/app/issues/1992) and
[API #848](https://github.com/recoupable/api/pull/848); it is not delivery of every
former capability. An agent or local skill may help prepare inputs, but that
does not establish a hosted route or compatibility with the former request.

This is a reference correction. No provider run or audio-quality check was
performed to make these availability statements.


# Get Artist Posts

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/posts/get

Retrieve all social media posts from an artist across all platforms. This endpoint aggregates posts from all connected social media profiles for the specified artist, newest first. Engagement counts (`views`, `likes`, `comments`, `reposts`) are the values captured by the most recent scrape of that profile; they are null on platforms that do not report them and on posts stored before engagement capture. Supports pagination for large post collections.

## GET /api/artists/{id}/posts

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/social.json

# Social Scrape

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/social/scrape

Trigger a scrape of one social profile. Use [Get Artist Socials](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/artists/socials) first to get the social `id`. The response contains scraper run metadata; poll it with the [Scraper Results API](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/apify/scraper).

## POST /api/socials/{id}/scrape

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/social.json

## Authentication

This operation requires one of the security alternatives in the specification below. Security scheme definitions are included where present in the published specification.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

# api-reference/artist/socials-scrape

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/artist/socials-scrape

Trigger scrape jobs for all social profiles linked to an artist. Returns a runId per social profile that you can poll for status and results via the [Scraper Results API](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/apify/scraper).

## POST /api/artist/socials/scrape

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/releases.json

# Search

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/spotify/search

Search for artists, albums, tracks, and playlists using the Spotify API. This endpoint is a proxy to the official Spotify Search API.

## GET /api/spotify/search

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/social.json

## Authentication

The supplied specification does not declare an OpenAPI security object for this operation. Its declared headers and parameters still apply. Consult the authentication guide and the full specification before calling it.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

## Operation and referenced schemas

```json
{
  "openapi": "3.1.0",
  "info": {
    "title": "Recoup API - Social",
    "description": "API documentation for the Recoup platform - an AI agent platform for the music industry",
    "license": {
      "name": "MIT"
    },
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "servers": [
    {
      "url": "https://api.recoupable.dev"
    }
  ],
  "paths": {
    "/api/spotify/search": {
      "get": {
        "operationId": "getSpotifySearch",
        "description": "Search for artists, albums, tracks, and playlists using the Spotify API. This endpoint is a proxy to the official Spotify Search API.",
        "parameters": [
          {
            "name": "q",
            "in": "query",
            "description": "The search query keywords and optional field filters",
            "required": true,
            "schema": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "type",
            "in": "query",
            "description": "A comma-separated list of item types to search across: album, artist, playlist, track, show, episode, audiobook",
            "required": true,
            "schema": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "market",
            "in": "query",
            "description": "An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code or 'from_token'",
            "required": false,
            "schema": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "limit",
            "in": "query",
            "description": "Maximum number of results to return (default: 20, min: 1, max: 50)",
            "required": false,
            "schema": {
              "type": "integer",
              "default": 20,
              "minimum": 1,
              "maximum": 50
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "offset",
            "in": "query",
            "description": "The index of the first result to return (default: 0, max: 10000)",
            "required": false,
            "schema": {
              "type": "integer",
              "default": 0,
              "maximum": 10000
            }
          }
        ],
        "responses": {
          "200": {
            "description": "Search results retrieved successfully",
            "content": {
              "application/json": {
                "schema": {
                  "$ref": "#/components/schemas/SpotifySearchResponse"
                }
              }
            }
          },
          "400": {
            "description": "Bad request - missing required parameters",
            "content": {
              "application/json": {
                "schema": {
                  "$ref": "#/components/schemas/SpotifyErrorResponse"
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "components": {
    "schemas": {
      "SpotifySearchResponse": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "artists": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/SpotifyArtistsPaginated",
            "description": "Search results for artists (if type includes artist)"
          },
          "albums": {
            "type": "object",
            "description": "Search results for albums (if type includes album)"
          },
          "tracks": {
            "type": "object",
            "description": "Search results for tracks (if type includes track)"
          },
          "playlists": {
            "type": "object",
            "description": "Search results for playlists (if type includes playlist)"
          }
        }
      },
      "SpotifyErrorResponse": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "error": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "status": {
                "type": "integer",
                "description": "HTTP status code"
              },
              "message": {
                "type": "string",
                "description": "Error message"
              }
            },
            "description": "Error details"
          }
        }
      },
      "SpotifyArtistsPaginated": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "href": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "A link to the Web API endpoint returning the full result"
          },
          "items": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "$ref": "#/components/schemas/SpotifyArtistObject"
            },
            "description": "List of artist objects"
          },
          "limit": {
            "type": "integer",
            "description": "The maximum number of items in the response"
          },
          "next": {
            "type": "string",
            "nullable": true,
            "description": "URL to the next page of items"
          },
          "offset": {
            "type": "integer",
            "description": "The offset of the items returned"
          },
          "previous": {
            "type": "string",
            "nullable": true,
            "description": "URL to the previous page of items"
          },
          "total": {
            "type": "integer",
            "description": "The total number of items available"
          }
        }
      },
      "SpotifyArtistObject": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "external_urls": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/SpotifyExternalUrls"
          },
          "followers": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/SpotifyFollowers"
          },
          "genres": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "string"
            },
            "description": "A list of the genres the artist is associated with"
          },
          "href": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "A link to the Web API endpoint providing full details"
          },
          "id": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The Spotify ID for the artist"
          },
          "images": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "$ref": "#/components/schemas/SpotifyImage"
            },
            "description": "Images of the artist in various sizes"
          },
          "name": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The name of the artist"
          },
          "popularity": {
            "type": "integer",
            "description": "The popularity of the artist (0-100)"
          },
          "type": {
            "type": "string",
            "enum": [
              "artist"
            ],
            "description": "The object type, always 'artist'"
          },
          "uri": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The Spotify URI for the artist"
          }
        }
      },
      "SpotifyExternalUrls": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "spotify": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "The Spotify URL for the object"
          }
        }
      },
      "SpotifyFollowers": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "href": {
            "type": "string",
            "nullable": true,
            "description": "This will always be set to null"
          },
          "total": {
            "type": "integer",
            "description": "The total number of followers"
          }
        }
      },
      "SpotifyImage": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "url": {
            "type": "string",

          },
          "height": {
            "type": "integer",
```

# Songs by ISRC

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/apple/songs

Look up recordings in the Apple Music catalog by ISRC. Accepts up to 25 comma-separated ISRCs per request and returns one row per **requested** ISRC, so a recording that Apple does not carry comes back explicitly as `found: false` rather than being omitted. Complements `GET /api/spotify/search`, which reaches ISRCs only through a fuzzy `isrc:` search query; Apple matches the identifier exactly and additionally returns release-level rights metadata (`upc`, `record_label`, `copyright`) that Spotify does not expose.

## GET /api/apple/songs

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/social.json

## Authentication

This operation requires one of the security alternatives in the specification below. Security scheme definitions are included where present in the published specification.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

## Operation and referenced schemas

```json
{

    {

  "paths": {
    "/api/apple/songs": {

        "description": "Look up recordings in the Apple Music catalog by ISRC. # Agents
```

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/agents

Verified email onboarding for a separate Recoup REST API key.

## Use your real account

Prefer [MCP OAuth](https://recoupable.dev/docs/mcp-oauth) for supported AI hosts. REST integrations need a
separate API key; an OAuth connection does not export one into your shell.

Use the email verification flow below with an address the user controls. Keep
the returned key out of messages and logs, and store it through a secret facility
or an explicitly approved local environment file. Never use a disposable account
to recover an existing user's data.

The source signup contract also supports immediate keys for new `agent+` addresses.
That creates a separate identity; it does not grant customer or organization access.
It is not the recommended onboarding path for customer work. Multiple API keys per
account are supported, without revoking existing keys.

## Standard signup (email verification)

If you're building a human-facing integration and want the user to verify their real email, use an email address the user controls:

Step 1 — request a verification code:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/agents/signup" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "you@example.com"}'
```

Step 2 — submit the 6-digit code from the verification email:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/agents/verify" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "you@example.com", "code": "123456"}'
```

Response:

```json
{
  "account_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "api_key": "recoup_sk_abc123...",
  "message": "Verified"
}
```

## Using your API key

Pass the returned `api_key` in the `x-api-key` header on every authenticated request:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/tasks" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY"
```

See [Authentication](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication) for the full authentication model, including organization access and Bearer token support, and [Quickstart](https://recoupable.dev/docs/quickstart) for your first end-to-end request.


# Content Agent

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/content-agent

Use hosted creative presets and current image, video and composition primitives.

## Release Packs

For a song-centered content pack, use [Release Packs](https://recoupable.dev/docs/release-packs): collect
essential context inline, preserve one job, quote the complete scope and produce
reviewed media. New releases, catalog rediscovery, anniversaries, reissues and
remixes use the same brief-driven path. These pack operations do not require an
existing artist or repository; availability depends on deployed host tools.

## Hosted workflows

`POST /api/content/create` retains the hosted preset workflow. Supply the authorized
`artist_account_id`, optional `template`, `images`, `songs`, `batch` (defaults to 1; range 1–30), `lipsync`, `upscale`
and `caption_length`. Discover templates through `/api/content/templates` and its
detail route. The response contains `runIds`; poll `/api/tasks/runs?runId=...` until
terminal. Report failures and inspect the final artifact before delivery.

Hosted lipsync is a supported preset intent. The coordinated API/worker repair
restores the selected song window to the fixed audio-to-video path; that repaired
journey is release-pending until deployment and actual output verification.

## Direct primitives

For images use `POST /api/content/image` with `prompt` and up to 10 unique
`image_urls`. The house model is Muse Image, switching to its edit path when
references are present. New clients must use `image_urls`; compatibility aliases
are translated by the reconciliation release.

For video use `POST /api/content/video` with `prompt`, optional `image_url` and
`end_image_url`, integer `duration` 5–15, and `resolution` `480P` or `768P`.
The house model is MiniMax H3 Max. It has no six-mode selector, arbitrary model,
reference-only, extend, `video_url` or `audio_url` request control. Unsupported
semantic inputs return 400 in the reconciliation release, before paid generation.

The dedicated `/api/content/lipsync` primitive restores the existing fixed LTX
model for the worker; it is not assumed available on an older deployment.
Caption, transcribe, analyze, upscale and edit have their own endpoint contracts.
Local ffmpeg composition can crop, trim, overlay or mux a song; it does not create
mouth synchronization or prove a hosted generation succeeded.

## Cost and evidence

Each generation/inference stage can consume credits. `/api/content/estimate`
returns an advisory estimate, not a guaranteed price or complete final ledger.
A later failed composition does not imply that completed upstream work was free.
On insufficient credits, surface `billingUrl` and stop. Consult [Credits](https://recoupable.dev/docs/credits).

Record image inspection, motion review and audio playback. The worker checks for
an audio stream on lipsync output before composition; perceptual mouth alignment
still requires inspection. Automated checks do not replace human QA.

## Slack integration

The separate [Slack webhook](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/content-agent/webhook) handles
Content Agent mentions. Its request/event contract and the [completion callback](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/content-agent/callback) are distinct from direct primitives.
Workspace operators must configure the Slack application and service credentials;
installing a creative skill does not install that integration.

### Set up the Slack app

Create a Slack app, enable the `chat:write` and `app_mentions:read` bot scopes,
and subscribe to `app_mention` events at
`https://api.recoupable.dev/api/content-agent/slack`. Install it in the intended
workspace and invite it to the channel.

Configure `SLACK_CONTENT_BOT_TOKEN`, `SLACK_CONTENT_SIGNING_SECRET`,
`CODING_AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET` and `REDIS_URL` in the Recoup API service.
The existing Tasks worker uses the same `CODING_AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET` for
completion callbacks and its authorized Recoup credential and API base URL.
Keep these values in service secret settings. The current callback secret name
is `CODING_AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET`; `CONTENT_AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET` is obsolete.

Mention the installed bot with the authorized artist account UUID:

```text
@RecoupContentAgent ARTIST_ACCOUNT_UUID artist-caption-bedroom batch=1
```

The template, `batch=N` (1–30) and `lipsync` flags are optional. Check the
acknowledgment, then inspect the completed result or reported failure in the
thread. Generated output still requires the inspection described above.


# Release Packs

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/release-packs

Turn a song and a campaign occasion into a coherent set of reviewed music assets.

> **Info**
> This contract accompanies the Release Packs first-use rollout. Availability depends
> on the deployed API and the tools exposed by your connected host. A plugin download
> or successful sign-in alone does not establish that generation is available.

## Start with the music

Ask your agent: **“Create a release pack for this song.”** Supply the audio or an
accessible audio link. A listening page is not an audio file. Tell it whether this is a new release, an anniversary, a
reissue, a remix, or a catalog rediscovery campaign.

The agent reuses information you have already supplied and any selected, accessible
Recoup context. It asks only for essential gaps: the correct artist and recording,
the occasion, and artwork or creative direction. You can ask it to propose a
direction from the music instead. It must distinguish that proposal from your
established branding.

You do not need an existing artist profile, Spotify history, connected social
accounts, a catalog import, or a GitHub workspace to prepare a pack. An empty
Recoup roster is a valid new account. Sign in through your host's Recoup connection
when the agent needs authenticated execution; it should resume the same request.

**“Plan a release” is a different request.** It produces a creative brief and
rollout plan. Ask for a release pack to produce media, or ask for both so the agent
can carry the same brief into production.

When ChatGPT supplies a selected attachment to the upload tool, the tool accepts
its host file reference directly. It imports the selected download URL into
private Recoup storage and validates the actual media bytes. Other hosts can use
the supported source URL, inline or signed-upload modes; a filename alone is not
an accessible recording.

For direct API uploads, small inline files are limited to approximately 3 MB
(4,000,000 base64 characters). For normal song files, request a private signed
upload, transfer the file and finalize it, or import an accessible HTTPS source
up to 50 MiB for audio or 10 MiB for a reference image. Supported transfers depend on your host; an attachment is usable
only after the agent can access its actual bytes. Audio formats include MP3,
WAV, FLAC and M4A. Source images can be PNG, JPEG or WebP.

## What the brief contains

| Input | How it is used |
| --- | --- |
| Artist, song and exact version | Keep the recording, remix and artist identity consistent |
| Real audio and selected hook | Put the correct music into the finished clips |
| Occasion | Choose relevant concepts and copy rather than defaulting to “out now” |
| Creative direction or references | Keep a coherent visual family and voice |
| Primary action and destination | Write relevant captions without inventing links |
| Audience, platforms and constraints | Choose useful formats and respect supplied boundaries |

For anniversaries, the original release date and campaign date are separate. If
the original date is unknown, the agent must obtain it before making dated
anniversary claims. A catalog request needs a bounded selection of recordings;
it must not silently generate a pack for every track.

Research enriches the brief. Missing research or audience metrics should not
force unrelated onboarding or fabricated statistics. Existing artwork and
supplied preferences can be enough to propose strong creative work. An artist's
face is optional; artwork-led and typographic work are valid directions.

## Scope and budget before generation

### Save a direction and choose how involved to be

Connections exposing `brief.creative_context` can save an established visual world,
a rough idea or an exploratory direction in the same pack. The field is optional;
older connections keep their existing brief behavior. It holds attributed references,
up to three direction candidates and the selected candidate.

**Run with it** uses `working_mode: "autonomous"`: the agent records its direction
selection and continues within the approved budget. **Show me directions first**
uses `working_mode: "guided"`: final quoting and generation wait for a selection
recorded from the customer's feedback. An agent's own choice does not count as
customer selection in guided mode.

Save candidates under `directions`, then record `selection.direction_id`,
`selection.selected_by` (`customer` or `agent`) and a short `decision_note`.
Direction and reference IDs must be unique within this brief; selections cannot
point to another pack's candidate. Updating these fields follows the same saved
job and expected-revision rules and invalidates its earlier quote.

A reference manifest item declares its source, media type and `usage`:
`reference_only` is inspiration, while `production` explicitly makes an image
eligible as a selected generation input. Only production images referenced by
the chosen direction enter the renderer. Together with explicit legacy
`reference_image_urls`, at most five distinct production images are supported.
The original source manifest stays unchanged when production inputs are resolved.

This first slice accepts supplied direction boards through an optional `board_url`.
It does not add automatic mood-board generation, public-profile harvesting or new
asset types. Discover those capabilities before promising them. An optional
customer checkpoint does not authorize additional spending or publication.

Preparation and generation are separate operations. Before paid production, the
agent shows the proposed direction, deliverables, cost scope and maximum budget.
The quote binds the current brief and deliverables. Changing the song or scope
requires a new quote; an earlier approval cannot silently authorize different work.

The default scope is 15 creative pieces: eight video clips, four quote cards, one
artwork, one carousel and one visualizer, with captions. A carousel is one piece;
its slides and alternate aspect ratios are identified as components or variants.
You can request a smaller scope. The quote must describe the actual selected work,
including chargeable stages and any retry allowance. Current quotes charge for
image and motion generation; captioning, audio analysis, composition and inspection
are included without an added customer fee. The approved amount is held before
production; unused stages are refunded. A new paid retry needs its own quote.

The older `GET /api/content/estimate` is an advisory per-video estimate. It is not
a complete Release Packs quote. On insufficient credits the agent surfaces the
returned `billingUrl`; it must not buy credits, switch accounts or retry paid
generation automatically.

## One job, with visible progress

The pack retains its brief, revision, quote, individual asset states and completed
work. Signing in, waiting for a render, or recovering from a failed stage should
not make you repeat the request or regenerate the whole pack.

The first representative asset is produced and inspected early. The agent then
continues the agreed batch within your budget, unless you requested a preview
checkpoint. Progress distinguishes requested, generated, inspected and delivered
assets. A partly generated pack is reported as partial.

## Review and delivery

A finished music-bearing asset must contain the selected recording and the correct
audio window. Inspection covers sound, timing, duration, framing, readable text,
visual consistency and the campaign brief. A render request, a prompt or a concept
is not a finished asset. Static image inspection and video inspection are separate.

Delivery includes previews, usable files, captions, a manifest and any unresolved
gaps. The agent retains successful work when a stage fails and retries only within
the approved scope and budget. Release Packs stops at the assets: posting and
scheduling need a separate request.

After delivery, you can save confirmed artist preferences for next time. A
one-off creative proposal must not overwrite established branding or become a
permanent public knowledge-base entry automatically.

## API and connected tools

Connected operations are `prepare_release_pack`, `get_release_pack`,
`estimate_release_pack`, `generate_release_pack`, `retry_release_pack`,
`upload_release_pack_asset` and `export_release_pack`. Discover their actual schemas
in the connected host; older connections may need a refresh.

The shared API contract separates preparation, reading, quoting, generation,
retry and selected-asset upload. Connected tools use the same account and job
rules. Credentials remain with the host; an agent must not extract OAuth tokens
into REST requests or ask for an API key to compensate for a missing MCP tool.

If a required operation is unavailable, the agent should name that operation,
retain the brief and explain the next step. It must not claim the entire account
is disconnected or present a plan as completed media.

# Get Tasks

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/tasks/get

# Create Task

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/tasks/create

Create a new scheduled task that runs a prompt against an artist on a recurring cron schedule. The response matches the [GET endpoint](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/tasks/get) (a `TasksResponse` with the created task in the `tasks` array).

## POST /api/tasks

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/releases.json

## Authentication

The supplied specification does not declare an OpenAPI security object for this operation. Its declared headers and parameters still apply. Consult the authentication guide and the full specification before calling it.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

# Slack Webhook

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/content-agent/webhook

Webhook endpoint for the Recoup Content Agent Slack bot. Receives @mention events from Slack and triggers content generation for the mentioned artist. The bot parses the mention text for `<artist_account_id> [template] [batch=N] [lipsync]`, validates the artist, calls POST /api/content/create, and starts a background polling task that reports results back to the Slack thread.

## POST /api/content-agent/{platform}

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/content.json

## Authentication

The supplied specification does not declare an OpenAPI security object for this operation. Its declared headers and parameters still apply. Consult the authentication guide and the full specification before calling it.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

## Operation and referenced schemas

```json

    "title": "Recoup API - Content",

      "name": "MIT"
    },
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "servers": [
    {
      "url": "https://api.recoupable.dev"
    }
```

# Create Sandbox

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/sandboxes/create

Create a new ephemeral sandbox environment. Optionally executes a command or an OpenCode prompt if provided. Sandboxes are isolated Linux microVMs that can be used to evaluate account-generated code, run AI agent output safely, or execute reproducible tasks. The sandbox will automatically stop after the timeout period. If no command or prompt is provided, the sandbox is created without triggering any background task. Use the prompt parameter as a shortcut to run `opencode run "<prompt>"` in the sandbox. Pass account_id to create a sandbox for a specific account the API key has access to. Authentication is handled via the x-api-key header or Authorization Bearer token.

## POST /api/sandboxes

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/content.json

## Authentication

The supplied specification does not declare an OpenAPI security object for this operation. Its declared headers and parameters still apply. Consult the authentication guide and the full specification before calling it.

# Update Snapshot

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/sandboxes/snapshot

Set a custom snapshot ID for an account. By default, updates the key owner's account. Pass account_id to target a specific account the API key has access to. This allows accounts to use a specific sandbox snapshot when creating new sandboxes, enabling reproducible environments with pre-configured tools, dependencies, and files.

## PATCH /api/sandboxes

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/content.json

# Upload Files

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/sandboxes/upload-files

Upload one or more files to the authenticated account's Git-backed repository. Each file URL is committed separately; paths inside a submodule resolve to that repository. Authenticate with `x-api-key` or an Authorization Bearer token.

## POST /api/sandboxes/files

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/content.json

## Authentication

The supplied specification does not declare an OpenAPI security object for this operation. Its declared headers and parameters still apply. Consult the authentication guide and the full specification before calling it.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

## Operation and referenced schemas

```json
{
  "openapi": "3.1.0",
  "info": {
    "title": "Recoup API - Content",
    "description": "API documentation for the Recoup platform - an AI agent platform for the music industry",
    "license": {
      "name": "MIT"
    },
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "servers": [
    {
      "url": "https://api.recoupable.dev"
    }
  ],
  "paths": {
    "/api/sandboxes/files": {
      "post": {
        "operationId": "postSandboxesFiles",
        "description": "Upload one or more files to the authenticated account's Git-backed repository. Each file URL is committed separately; paths inside a submodule resolve to that repository. Authenticate with `x-api-key` or an Authorization Bearer token.\n\nFor a guarded update of an existing file:\n1. Read it with `GET /api/sandboxes/file?include_revision=true` and retain the returned `sha` with that draft.\n2. Upload the edited bytes using the [staged-file upload](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/sandboxes/stage-file), then send the resulting URL and the original SHA as `files[].expected_sha`. Guarded updates save to `main`. A conflicting save is not retried automatically.\n3. On a conflict, preserve the unsaved draft, reread the latest content and reconcile explicitly. Do not fetch a new SHA merely to force an older draft through.\n\nA batch is not a transaction. HTTP 200 can include successful `uploaded` receipts alongside `errors` and `conflicts`; inspect every file. If every upload fails only because its condition conflicts, the response is 409. If all fail with mixed conflict/other failures, it is 500 and keeps the conflicts list. Conflicts contain submitted file names; successes include resulting blob SHAs.\n\nTemporary upload blobs are deleted after every attempt, including conflicts, so retrying requires a new upload URL. Omitting `expected_sha` creates or updates the file on the repository default branch without checking the version you opened. The condition only supports updates to existing files. It protects saves that supply it; saving here does not update files in an already running sandbox.\n\nIf the target was deleted after the read, do not retry without the condition. This upload has no dedicated missing-target status: non-conflict failures return 500 when no file succeeds, or appear in `errors` alongside successful receipts in a 200 partial result. A missing target is not guaranteed to return 404 or 409; reread the path before deciding how to recover.",
        "requestBody": {
          "description": "JSON body containing file URLs and target path",
          "required": true,
          "content": {
            "application/json": {
              "schema": {
                "$ref": "#/components/schemas/UploadSandboxFilesRequest"
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "responses": {
          "200": {
            "description": "At least one file was saved. Partial success also returns errors and optional conflicts; keep every successful receipt and inspect every failure.",
            "content": {
              "application/json": {
                "schema": {
                  "$ref": "#/components/schemas/UploadSandboxFilesResponse"
                },
                "examples": {
                  "success": {
                    "summary": "All requested files saved",
                    "value": {
                      "status": "success",
                      "uploaded": [
                        {
                          "path": "drafts/notes.txt",
                          "sha": "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"
                        }
                      ]
                    }
                  },
                  "partialConflict": {
                    "summary": "One file saved and another conflicted",
                    "value": {
                      "status": "success",
                      "uploaded": [
                        {
                          "path": "drafts/saved.txt",
                          "sha": "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"
                        }
                      ],
                      "errors": [
                        "notes.txt: File changed"
                      ],
                      "conflicts": [
                        "notes.txt"
                      ]
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
            }
```

# Create Account

# Create Subscription Session

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/subscriptions/sessions-create

Create a checkout session to start a subscription for the authenticated account. Returns a hosted checkout URL that the client should redirect to. `plan` picks the price: `pro` (default) is pre-configured with a 30-day trial period; `starter` is charged at checkout with no trial.

## POST /api/subscriptions/sessions

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

## Authentication

The supplied specification does not declare an OpenAPI security object for this operation. Its declared headers and parameters still apply. Consult the authentication guide and the full specification before calling it.

```json
    {
      "url": "https://api.recoupable.dev"

  ],
  "paths": {
    "/api/subscriptions/sessions": {
      "post": {
        "operationId": "postSubscriptionsSessions",
        "description": "Create a checkout session to start a subscription for the authenticated account. # Claim Subscription
```

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/subscriptions/claim-create

Attach a subscription bought through [Create Subscription Session](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/subscriptions/sessions-create) (anonymous path) to the authenticated account. Needed only when the signed-in email differs from the email typed into Stripe Checkout; when they match, the webhook already linked the subscription and this call is a no-op that returns 200.

## POST /api/subscriptions/claim

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

## Authentication

This operation requires one of the security alternatives in the specification below. Security scheme definitions are included where present in the published specification.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

## Operation and referenced schemas

```json

  "openapi": "3.1.0",

      "name": "MIT"
    },

  },
  "servers": [
    {
      "url": "https://api.recoupable.dev"
    }
  ],
  "paths": {
    "/api/subscriptions/claim": {
      "post": {
        "operationId": "postSubscriptionsClaim",
        "description": "Attach a subscription bought through [Create Subscription Session](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/subscriptions/sessions-create) (anonymous path) to the authenticated account. Needed only when the signed-in email differs from the email typed into Stripe Checkout; when they match, the webhook already linked the subscription and this call is a no-op that returns 200.",
        "security": [
          {
            "apiKeyAuth": []

        "type": "object",
        "required": [
```

# Get Account Subscription

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/subscription-get

Retrieve the subscription that confers an account's plan, directly or via an organization: `isPro`, `status`, `plan`, `source`, plus the billing fields `name`, `amountCents`, `currency`, `interval`, `collectionMethod` and `currentPeriodEnd`. Everything but `isPro` and `status` is null when `status` is `none`. `id` may be the authenticated account or an organization the caller belongs to.

# Create Billing Portal Session

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/portal-create

Create a Stripe Customer Portal session for an account. Returns a hosted URL where the customer can update the card on file, view invoices, or cancel a Starter or Pro subscription; the client should redirect the user to that URL. The portal opens on the Stripe customer that owns the account's active subscription, so accounts without an active subscription get a 400 even when a tagged customer with a card exists. `id` may be the authenticated account or an organization the caller belongs to. Enterprise (invoiced) plans are managed with your Recoup contact and the app does not offer this portal for them, but the endpoint works for any account with an active subscription.

## POST /api/accounts/{id}/portal

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

## Authentication

This operation requires one of the security alternatives in the specification below. Security scheme definitions are included where present in the published specification.

# Get Default Payment Method

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/payment-method-get

Retrieve the default payment method on file for an account. An account may be tagged on more than one Stripe customer (for example an organization whose card was saved on one customer and whose invoiced plan lives on another); the card is read from the tagged customer that holds a default payment method. Returns `card: null` when the selected customer has no supported default card, including when no tagged customer exists — the top-up dialog uses this to decide whether to show a pre-charge confirmation (card present) or route to a checkout session to collect one (`card: null`). Cards are returned even when expired; callers should compare `exp_month` / `exp_year` against the current date and warn the customer, since an off-session charge against an expired card will decline. Removing the selected card does not remove other saved cards: a later read can select a different remaining card. Auto top-up stays off after successful removal until explicitly re-enabled.

## GET /api/accounts/{id}/payment-method

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

## Authentication

This operation requires one of the security alternatives in the specification below. Security scheme definitions are included where present in the published specification.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

# Save a Payment Method

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/payment-method-create

Create a $0 card-on-file checkout session for an account. Stripe `setup` mode saves a payment method without charging anything or starting a subscription; the saved card becomes the account's default and is what credit purchases and auto top-up charge. The card is saved on the account's Stripe customer that already holds a default card, or the newest tagged customer; a customer is created (and tagged with the account id) if none exists yet. Returns a hosted checkout URL that the client should redirect to. `id` may be the authenticated account or an organization the caller belongs to.

## POST /api/accounts/{id}/payment-method

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

## Authentication

This operation requires one of the security alternatives in the specification below. Security scheme definitions are included where present in the published specification.

# Remove the Payment Method

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/payment-method-delete

Turn off automatic credit top-ups for the authorized account, then detach its selected default card. This removes one card selected from the account's tagged Stripe customers; it does not delete every saved card. A successful request returns 204 with no response body. `id` may be the authenticated account or an organization the caller belongs to.

# List Account Payments

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/payments-get

List the invoices paid or owed by an account, newest first: subscription renewals, credit purchases, and invoiced enterprise plans alike. Invoices are merged across every Stripe customer tagged with the account id, so a card saved on one customer and an invoiced plan on another appear in one list. Non-draft rows carry the hosted invoice URL for the receipt; `url` is null for drafts. Returns an empty list (not 404) when the account has no tagged Stripe customer or no invoices yet. `startingAfter` is an invoice id from a previous page; the next page holds invoices created before it. `id` may be the authenticated account or an organization the caller belongs to.

## GET /api/accounts/{id}/payments

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

# Get Auto Top-up Settings

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/auto-top-up-get

Read the auto top-up settings for an account. Auto top-up is opt-in: it is off for every account until the account turns it on and chooses both the amount to buy and the balance that triggers it. When it is on, the api charges the default card on file for `amountCents` the first time a credit deduction leaves the balance below `thresholdCents`, then grants the credits and emails a receipt. `id` may be the authenticated account or an organization the caller belongs to.

## GET /api/accounts/{id}/auto-top-up

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

# Update Auto Top-up Settings

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/auto-top-up-update

Set the auto top-up settings for an account. All three fields are required on every call; there is no partial update. Turning it on requires a card on file (`GET /api/accounts/{id}/payment-method` returns a card), an amount between 5.00 and 1,000.00 USD, and a threshold below the amount. Turning it off keeps the last amount and threshold so the account can turn it back on without retyping them. Guardrails that apply once it is on: at most one top-up per account per 10 minutes; a card decline turns `enabled` back to `false`, records `lastError`, and emails the account instead of retrying; a successful selected-card removal turns it off before detachment, even when other saved cards remain. Removal does not cancel a charge already in progress. `id` may be the authenticated account or an organization the caller belongs to.

## PUT /api/accounts/{id}/auto-top-up

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

## Authentication

This operation requires one of the security alternatives in the specification below. Security scheme definitions are included where present in the published specification.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

# Get Account Credits

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/credits-get

Retrieve the current credit balance for an account. Returns the remaining credits along with the plan-derived monthly total and used count, plus a flag indicating whether the account is on a pro plan (directly or via an organization). # Get Account Usage

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/usage-get

List the charges that consumed an account's credits: one line item per deduction from `usage_events`, newest first, over a period. Each item carries the amount as the raw ledger integer (`credits_deducted`, micro-dollars: 1,000,000 = $1.00) and the same amount formatted as a dollar string (`usd`), and the response carries the total for the whole period, not just the page. Access is the same as [`GET /api/accounts/{id}/credits`](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/accounts/credits-get): the authenticated account itself, or another account reachable through organization membership.

## GET /api/accounts/{id}/usage

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

## Authentication

This operation requires one of the security alternatives in the specification below. Security scheme definitions are included where present in the published specification.

[Authentication guide](https://recoupable.dev/docs/authentication)

# Update Pulse

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/pulses/update

## PATCH /api/pulses

# Add Organization Domain

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/organizations/add-domain

Map an email domain to an organization for automatic membership. After mapping, any account that signs up (or signs in) with an email at this domain is automatically added to the organization. A domain can belong to at most one organization.  This endpoint is idempotent - re-adding the same domain to the same organization returns the existing mapping.

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

```json
        "description": "Map an email domain to an organization for automatic membership.           "200": {
```

# Admin signup report availability

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/admins/agent-signups

The former admin signup-report route is not available; reporting access still needs a product decision.

`GET /api/admins/agent/signups` is not available. There is no implemented
replacement for the old per-signup report in the current platform API.

[Agent signup and email verification](https://recoupable.dev/docs/agents) are account-onboarding flows,
not reporting APIs. Creating an account or API key does not grant access to
other accounts' signup records.

## Unfinished product decision

[Reconciliation #327](https://github.com/recoupable/mono/issues/327) retains the
decision about who should see this report, whether it needs individual records
or aggregate counts, and which time windows and identifying fields are allowed.
No reporting API or permission policy is being introduced by this documentation
correction. The former request and response are removed from the callable
specification until the owning product decision and implementation exist.

# Credit Usage Rollup (Admin)

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/admins/credits-rollup

Returns the per-account rollup of credit usage over the selected period, sorted by total credits deducted descending. Each row carries the account identity (UUID + display name + primary email) and the aggregated spend so the admin dashboard can render a top-spenders table without joining client-side. Pair with [`GET /api/admins/credits/events?account_id=…&period=…`](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/admins/credits-events) to drill into the individual `usage_events` rows for a single account. Requires the authenticated account to be a Recoup admin.

## GET /api/admins/credits/rollup

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

## Authentication

# Credit Usage Events (Admin)

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/admins/credits-events

Returns the raw `usage_events` rows for a single account over the selected period, sorted by `created_at` descending. Powers the drilldown view that expands when a row in the [`/api/admins/credits/rollup`](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/admins/credits-rollup) table is opened. Each event represents one debit (main agent turn, subagent step, chat completion, or research call), with token counts and `credits_deducted` matching the wallet drop on `credits_usage` for that account.

## GET /api/admins/credits/events

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/accounts.json

# Connection Ownership

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/connectors/ownership

The connector connection-ownership and authority contract: who owns a connection, who can act through it, and why roster membership never grants execute rights.

## Overview

Connectors link third-party services (Google Sheets, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, and others) to Recoup so agents can act on an artist's behalf. This page defines the **ownership and authority contract** for those connections: who a connection belongs to, and who is allowed to authorize, execute through, or disconnect it.

This contract is the source of truth for connector access control. Endpoint request and response shapes are documented separately in the [Connectors API reference](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/connectors/list).

---

## Association ≠ Authority

Artists in Recoup are **canonical and shared**. The same artist can appear in many accounts' rosters and in multiple organizations. Being associated with an artist is not the same as having authority to act through that artist's connections:

- An artist appearing in an account's roster (`account_artist_ids`) grants **read and analytics access only**.
- An artist appearing in an organization's roster likewise grants **read and analytics access only** to org members.
- Neither form of association ever grants the right to authorize, execute, or disconnect a connection.

> **Warning**
> Roster membership never inherits connection authority. If Account A connects an artist's TikTok, Account B having that same artist on its roster does **not** let Account B post through that connection.

---

## Connection Scope

Connections are scoped to the **relationship between an owner and an artist**, not to the bare canonical artist:

| Connection type | Scoped to |
| --- | --- |
| Personal | The `(account, artist)` pair |
| Org-shared | The `(organization, artist)` pair |

The connection is keyed on the **join row** (the specific account-to-artist or org-to-artist relationship), never on the canonical artist alone. Two accounts that both roster the same artist hold two independent connection scopes for that artist.

**Whoever establishes a connection owns it.** Ownership is set at authorization time and does not transfer through roster changes.

Because artists stay canonical and shared, **isolation lives on the connection**: sharing an artist across accounts and orgs is safe precisely because each connection is confined to the relationship that created it.

---

## Authority Matrix

| Capability | Who has it |
| --- | --- |
| Read / analytics on an artist | Any account or org member with the artist in their roster |
| Authorize a new connection | The account (or org member, for org-shared) establishing the connection, who then owns it |
| Execute actions through a connection | The owning account only; for org-shared connections, members of the owning org |
| Disconnect a connection | The owning account only; for org-shared connections, members of the owning org |
| Admin override | Recoup staff only (admins of the Recoup internal organization) |

> **Note**
> The admin override exists for support and abuse response. No customer account or organization, regardless of roster or org membership, can override another owner's connection.

---

## Relationship to the Current API Reference

The [Connectors endpoint reference](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/connectors/list) currently describes connections as scoped to the authenticated account alone. That reflects behavior that shipped before this contract; the API is being re-keyed to the per-`(account, artist)` / per-`(organization, artist)` model defined here. Where the two disagree, **this page is the authority contract**. Endpoint docs will be updated as the re-keyed API ships.

Endpoint request and response shapes for the re-keyed model are deliberately not documented here yet.

# List Connector Actions

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/connectors/list-actions

List the executable actions available across the authenticated account's connectors. Each action is a single tool that can be invoked via POST /api/connectors/actions — for example, the `googlesheets` connector exposes actions like `GOOGLESHEETS_WRITE_SPREADSHEET`. Actions whose parent connector is not yet connected are returned with `isConnected: false` and cannot be executed until the connector is authorized via POST /api/connectors.

## GET /api/connectors/actions

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/social.json

# Execute Connector Action

Source: https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/connectors/execute-action

Execute a connector action with the given parameters. The `actionSlug` must come from a prior call to GET /api/connectors/actions, and `parameters` must match the `parameters` JSON Schema returned for that action. The action's parent connector must be currently connected (`isConnected: true` in the catalog) — otherwise this endpoint returns 409. The `result` field passes through whatever the underlying connector returns; its shape is action-specific. To attach an image to a `file_uploadable` parameter (e.g. `images`), first stage it with [Upload Connector File](https://recoupable.dev/docs/api-reference/connectors/upload-file) and pass the returned descriptor.

## POST /api/connectors/actions

Full OpenAPI specification: https://recoupable.dev/docs/spec/social.json

The balance is checked here, so an account without enough credits gets **402** and no post is created. The charge is made only when the post reaches `posted`: a post that ends `failed` or `cancelled` is never charged. A scheduled post is checked against the balance when it is created and charged when it goes live.",

```json
          {
            "apiKeyAuth": []

            "bearerAuth": []
          }
```
